items.title: Society of Authors withdraws from Ethical AI Charter after member backlash
items.excerpt: The Society of Authors has withdrawn from the Ethical AI Charter it launched last week, following member backlash and a clarifying statement from CEO Anna Ganley on its position on generative AI.

items.title: An editor's first read must not be outsourced to AI
items.excerpt: Copy editor Adnan Algın argues that used too early, AI can suppress an editor's vital but indefinable first-read instincts on a manuscript.

items.title: Thélyson Orélien denies using AI to write novel but admits to plagiarism in earlier work
items.excerpt: Canadian author Thélyson Orélien denied using AI to write his prize-shortlisted novel C'était ça ou mourir, while admitting to 'unacceptable' plagiarism in earlier work. (Superseded 10-21 by publisher Boréal confirming AI use — see CBC/Yonhap.)

items.title: Survey Finds Book Buyers Split on AI Use
items.excerpt: A BookInsights.ai study finds younger readers more open to authors using AI in some form, but readers of all ages agree that books should disclose AI use.

items.title: Hundreds Sue Meta for Copyright Infringement, Rejecting Class Action Payouts
items.excerpt: Nearly 300 authors are suing Meta over AI training on pirated books, seeking a jury trial and the maximum $150,000 per infringement rather than class-action payouts; attorney Kyle Roche says many more cases are coming.

items.title: Publishers Are Splitting on AI While the Ground Shifts Everywhere Else
items.excerpt: Meta claims AI rights to publisher content while Google pays for it — publishers are diverging on licensing versus resisting AI use of their content.

items.title: From Content to Trusted Knowledge: Reflections on Frankfurt Book Fair 2026
items.excerpt: Reflections from Frankfurt 2026 on how publishers can turn trusted content into useful knowledge as AI systems and agents become the interface readers act through.

items.title: How AI Changes the Fundamental Structure of the Classroom—Especially the Segregated Ones
items.excerpt: A book excerpt examining how ChatGPT-era AI tools reshape reading, writing and instruction in American classrooms, and how they deepen gaps in segregated schools.

items.title: 佛공쿠르상 후보 제외된 소설 AI 대필 의혹 사실로…출판사 결별
items.excerpt: 캐나다 출판사 보레알이 신예 베스트셀러 작가 텔리송 오렐리앵의 인공지능(AI) 활용 의혹이 사실로 확인됐다며 작가와의 관계를 끝낸다고 밝혔다.

items.title: [단독] 한강·황석영 책 도둑질, 화웨이 등 中 AI기업도 가세했다
items.excerpt: 앤트로픽에 이어 중국 화웨이도 AI 모델 '판구 시그마' 학습에 한강·황석영 등 한국 작가의 책을 무단으로 내려받은 것으로 기술보고서를 통해 확인됐다.

items.title: “저작권 신탁기구 추진…AI의 ‘책 도둑질’ 막아야”
items.excerpt: 앤트로픽의 국내 도서 대량 매입·해적판 다운로드 논란 속에 한국출판인회의가 AI 학습 대응을 위한 저작권 신탁기구 설립을 추진한다고 밝혔다.

items.title: Publisher cuts ties with Quebec author accused of AI use in award-winning novel
items.excerpt: Éditions du Boréal said AI was used in Thélyson Orélien's novel C'était ça ou mourir, contrary to his denials, citing traces of AI tags in document metadata, and ended its relationship with the author.

items.title: The anti-AI writing police are everywhere. What are they looking for?
items.excerpt: Scandals over suspected AI use have spread across the writing industry this year; readers, prize judges and publishers struggle to verify whether words came from human effort or a machine prompt.

items.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
items.excerpt: After publishers and legal experts warned its new commercial terms were an AI-training power grab, Meta removed the word 'train' but still won't commit to respecting robots.txt.
